chunks: Zur'ah narrated from Samā'ah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله stood at Minā when he had completed his rites during the Farewell Hajj and said: 'O people, listen to what I say to you and understand it, for I do not know; perhaps I shall not meet you in this place after this year of ours.'"

Then he said: 'Which day is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This day.' He said: 'Then which month is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This month.' He said: 'Then which town is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This town.' He said: 'Then indeed your blood and your wealth are forbidden among you, like the sanctity of this day of yours in this month of yours in this land of yours, until the day you meet Him and He asks you about your deeds. Lo, have I conveyed?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'O Allah, bear witness. Lo, whoever has a trust with him, let him return it to the one who entrusted him with it, for indeed the blood of a Muslim man is not lawful for him, nor his wealth, except with the good pleasure of his own soul. So do not wrong yourselves, and do not return after me as disbelievers.'

key_terms.أَمَانَةٌ: a trust or entrusted property that must be returned
key_terms.بِطِيبَةِ نَفْسِهِ: with a person's willing consent and full satisfaction
key_terms.حَجَّةِ الْوَدَاعِ: the Farewell Pilgrimage of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.دِمَاءَكُمْ وَ أَمْوَالَكُمْ: your blood and your property, declared inviolable
key_terms.كُفَّارًا: disbelievers; here, a warning against reverting after him
key_terms.مَنَاسِكَهُ: the hajj rites that had been completed
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the sacred site where this address was delivered during hajj

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله teach in the Farewell Hajj about blood, wealth, and trusts?
ai.summary: This hadith records a solemn address of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله at Minā during the Farewell Hajj, emphasizing the inviolability of Muslim blood and property. It also commands the fulfillment of trusts, forbids wrongdoing, and frames these teachings within the sacredness of the time and place and the coming reckoning before Allah.
